solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Woman police sergeant given approval as a help to motorist

parts.note: Di is a woman's name, short for Diana
a tick is a mark of approval on work

explanation.surface: A female officer is praised for helping a stranded driver.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorist uses this graduated rod to check the oil level in the engine.

clue.text: Period of 31 days briefly needing help reportedly

parts.note: Dec is the short form of December, a month of 31 days

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word heard rather than seen

parts.note: aid is help

explanation.surface: Someone needs assistance for a month-long stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A ten-year span is a period of time.

clue.text: Within bowl shape one may have ground

definitions.text: Within bowl shape one may have ground

parts.words: Within bowl shape one may have ground
parts.note: a club-headed tool used inside a mortar, a bowl, to grind spices

explanation.surface: Inside a bowl-shaped space, a person could have some land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' reads as land, but it is the past of grind; the bowl is a mortar.
explanation.definitionFit: The kitchen tool paired with a mortar crushes things to powder within the bowl.

clue.text: Slab firm after what's on top has been removed

indicators.text: after what's on top has been removed
indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is taken off

parts.note: stable means firm

explanation.surface: A slab stays steady once its top layer is lifted.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat slab of stone or wood bearing an inscription is a tablet, or slab.

clue.text: Third-rate character facing defeat and packing up

parts.note: C is the grade for third-rate after A and B
losing is suffering defeat

explanation.surface: A mediocre person, facing a loss, calls it a day.
explanation.definitionFit: Packing up a business at the end of the day means shutting it, ending trade.

clue.text: Old king reversed statutes when pressed by old duke

indicators.note: the reversed word is squeezed between the two short pieces on either side of it
the word for statutes is read from right to left

parts.note: statutes are laws

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch overturns laws under pressure from an aged nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Oswald was a seventh-century king of Northumbria, later a saint, so an old king by name.

clue.text: Keep a close eye on man where ferries come in

parts.note: Stan is a man's name
Dover is the English Channel ferry port

explanation.surface: Someone is told to watch a man where the ferries dock.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand over someone is to supervise them closely, watching what they do.

clue.text: Element in a couple of drugs

parts.note: a statin is a cholesterol drug and E is ecstasy, two drugs

explanation.surface: A chemical element is present in two medicines.
explanation.definitionFit: Astatine is a rare radioactive chemical element, a halogen.

clue.text: What animal in accommodation knocked over mucky pile?

indicators.note: in a down clue knocked over means turned upside down, read bottom to top
in places the first pieces inside the accommodation

parts.note: a pad is slang for a home
eh is an exclamation like what?
a gnu is an animal, the wildebeest

explanation.surface: A puzzled cry: what creature in the lodgings toppled a messy heap?
explanation.definitionFit: A heap of manure is literally a pile of muck.

clue.text: Spooner's hit someone in the kitchen — volume of bread here

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two words for the next pieces trade their first letters

parts.note: to bash is to hit
a cook works in a kitchen

explanation.surface: Someone strikes the chef in the kitchen, where a loaf is mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bread' is slang for money, so a volume of bread is an accounts ledger.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledger recording money paid and received is a book for 'bread', slang for cash.

clue.text: Design not right for type of shoe

indicators.note: not here means without, so the letter for right is removed

parts.note: a pattern is a design

explanation.surface: A shoe style is described as a design that has gone wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A patten is an old overshoe raised on an iron ring to keep feet out of mud.

clue.text: Beautiful couple not quiet but loud

indicators.note: not marks the quiet letter as the one to go
but brings in the loud letter as its replacement

parts.note: a pair is a couple
p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet
f, forte, is the musical mark for loud

explanation.surface: A handsome couple who are noisy rather than quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair is an old word for beautiful, as in 'fair maiden'.

clue.text: Old and active, out for good times

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: A lively pensioner goes out for some fun.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian phrase, literally 'sweet life', means a life of luxurious pleasure.

clue.text: Get rid of pain having gone to doctor initially

indicators.note: the word for pain is attached after the doctor's letter
initially picks the first letter of doctor

parts.note: an itch is an irritating discomfort, a pain

explanation.surface: Someone's discomfort is cured after a visit to the doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: To ditch something is informally to abandon or discard it.

clue.text: Sell game that's gone over

indicators.note: gone over suggests turned over, so the game's name is read backwards

parts.note: golf is a game

explanation.surface: Someone sells a pastime that is past its best.
explanation.definitionFit: To flog is a British informal word for selling something.

clue.text: Introductory words from minister that should do for rustle and yap

indicators.note: to do for is to wreck, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A clergyman's opening words should silence rustling and chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister begins prayers with this formula inviting the congregation to pray.

clue.text: City artist, a man with a famous diagram secreted

indicators.note: secreted means hidden away, so the man is tucked inside the other letters

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
John Venn devised the Venn diagram

explanation.surface: An artist and a mathematician share a secret in some city.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravenna is a city in northern Italy famous for its Byzantine mosaics.

clue.text: Mother receives signal on time to gain impetus

indicators.note: receives means takes in, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: mum is mother
an omen is a sign or signal

explanation.surface: Mother gets a sign on time to build up speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Momentum is driving force, the impetus of something moving.

clue.text: Great desires evident in Conservative gibberish?

parts.note: ravings are wild, incoherent talk

explanation.surface: A Tory's wild nonsense betrays strong longings.
explanation.definitionFit: Cravings are strong yearnings, powerful wants.

clue.text: Physicist redoes experiment finally after botch-up

indicators.note: a botch-up is a mess, so the letters are scrambled
finally takes the last letter of experiment

explanation.surface: A scientist repeats a trial after a bungled first attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Hans Christian Oersted was the Danish physicist who discovered electromagnetism.

clue.text: Chop up diamonds and more diamonds

parts.note: D is the card abbreviation for diamonds
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone cuts up a hoard of gems, and then more gems.
explanation.definitionFit: To dice food is to cut it into small cubes.

clue.text: Fifty rods cast about — this fish must be caught!

indicators.note: cast about suggests the letters are thrown round to face the other way
the letters are caught inside the words Fifty rods

explanation.surface: An angler casts fifty fishing rods, determined to land a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The John Dory is an edible sea fish with a dark spot on each side.

clue.text: Toys — they shouldn't be dropped

definitions.meaning: in cricket a dolly is an easy catch that a fielder ought to hold

explanation.surface: Toys that children are warned not to drop.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket's 'dolly' is a gentle, simple catch.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolls are toys, and easy cricket catches must be held, never dropped.

clue.text: Cleaner, worker blankly incurious

parts.note: vac is short for vacuum cleaner
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: A cleaning employee stares with no interest at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacant look is empty, showing no thought or interest.

clue.text: Story that may be untrue on purpose

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
an end is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: A tale that could be a deliberate lie.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a traditional tale, possibly not historically true.

clue.text: 'andles mischievous kids?

indicators.note: the apostrophe shows the opening H dropped, as in Cockney speech

parts.note: helves are handles of axes or tools

explanation.surface: A Cockney grumbles about handling naughty children.
explanation.definitionFit: Elves are mischievous little sprites, so playfully a name for impish children.

clue.text: Nursery provision arrived — ancient father enthralled

indicators.note: enthralled means captivated, held inside, so the other pieces go within

parts.note: came means arrived
old means ancient
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest

explanation.surface: An elderly father turns up, captivated by a children's nursery.
explanation.definitionFit: In a plant nursery a glazed frame protects seedlings from the cold.

clue.text: Fine bird hobbling around?

parts.note: F is the pencil abbreviation for fine
a rail is a wading bird

explanation.surface: A fine bird limping about with an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: A weak elderly person might hobble about, being infirm.

clue.text: What 'arry has difficulty cracking? The reverse, that's plain

indicators.note: the reverse tells us to write the phrase backwards

parts.note: a Cockney 'Arry drops his H, so a hard nut becomes an 'ard nut

explanation.surface: Cockney Harry struggles to crack something; the opposite is obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain' looks like 'obvious', but it is the noun for flat land.
explanation.definitionFit: Tundra is a vast treeless Arctic plain.

clue.text: Go off course, eager to return to entrance

indicators.note: to return means going back, so the word for eager is read backwards

parts.note: avid means eager
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: Someone strays off the path, keen to get back to the way in.
explanation.definitionFit: To divagate is a formal word meaning to wander or stray from a route or subject.

clue.text: Model holds you back and saunters

indicators.note: holds means contains, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Kate Moss is a famous model

indicators.note: back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: A model clings to someone and strolls along.
explanation.definitionFit: To mosey is to walk in a leisurely, unhurried way, a synonym of strolling.

clue.text: One so behind had finally to be kept apart from others

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
late means behind time

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of had

explanation.surface: Someone running so late eventually had to be quarantined.
explanation.definitionFit: Something isolated is set apart and alone, separated from the rest.
